result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A cuts the required setup to a few basics and moves par levels, vendors, approvals, accounting and cycle counts to a checklist that stays on screen until each task is done, and it explains why. Answer B keeps all nine steps and only reorders and rewords them, which is exactly what rubric items 1 and 2 penalize. A has one small inconsistency: it calls locations required but still offers a skip, and its welcome line doesn't directly tie setup to placing a first order or counting a first item. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B changes what a new admin has to do before first use. It keeps a few short setup screens and moves par levels, vendors, approval rules, team invites, accounting and cycle counts to a checklist that stays visible until each task is done, and it explains why. Answer A only reorders and rewords the same nine steps; its main change is suggesting admins start par levels with their most-used items. B has a small inconsistency: it says 'two quick settings' but shows three setup screens. It also doesn't tie the first steps directly to placing a first order.
